_source: Phase 09 T1.3 rules profile: the constants that differ between the games (09-trilogy-matrix.md §2 rows marked 'each'). Constants that are the same in every game stay in Core code; DOS file-format facts stay in the codecs.
_gold: Manual p.10: 'A party can carry up to 65,000 GPs' and 'A bank account for a single character can hold a maximum of 65,000 GPs' (D-048). DOS clamps both at 65,535 (COM 0x2e5d); the excess is lost.
_guild: D-002: the manual's Guild holds 21 characters; DOS fills all 22 GUILD.DAT records, so the roster keeps 22 slots and original 22-character saves still load. Guild numbers slots+1..slots+3 are the elementals.
_guild_by_platform: T1.3 rest: what each original platform's Guild held (slots = record slots, max_characters = most characters N)EW fills). The remaster plays guild_slot_count / guild_max_characters above (D-002); this table only records the originals (RulesProfile.ForPlatform applies one). A platform or value no source states is left out [?]: Atari 8-bit, Atari ST, Mac and MSX (the combined I+II rulebook scan has no text layer, the text-layer I+II rulebook's Atari/Mac notes are silent, the Japanese MSX manual's OCR is unreadable), the Amiga's fillable maximum and the C64's slot count.
_starting_gold: Each new character starts with 256 GP in the bank (OV1 0x0BAC creation; manual: 256 GP each).
_original_platform: The platform whose code is I's rules source: the Original (DOS) preset reads guild_by_platform under this key (D-002).
_equipment_slots: 09 T2 (inventory-actions.md §2): the worn-item slots and the item ids each takes. Manual p.11: one weapon, armor and shield at a time; p.21-22 tables: shields 1-20, armor 21-40, weapons 41-100 (DOS kind letters S/A/W, OV1 0x17df).
_training: Guild training XP target constants (town-menus.md §Training, DOS OV1 0x11ea..0x12ab [C]): s = sum / divisor; F = 1.8^level, F = 1.0 when XP == 0. Play uses TownMenus.TrainingTarget (exact DOS doubles); this block states the same rule as profile data and a test pins the two together.

training._deltas: charisma_clamp: DOS clamps the price's 20 - CHA at 0 (OV1 0x13a1). spell_marks: a level-up marks the new level's spells only (OV1 0x9ee). hp_tie: an HP re-roll equal to the old maximum gives +1 (town-menus.md: roll > old).

_terrain: Wilderness terrain classes with a rule of their own (overworld-movement.md, OV2 0x5ea2): class 7 a certain fight once per trip against monster 12*T + 9 (0-based; tile 74 WARRIOR, 75 GREAT TROLL), class 10 swimming, class 11 the magical pool (the campaign). Every other class rolls Core's 0..99 random-encounter roll, < 6. Towns 40, inns 41, dungeons (class 5) and digits 6/7/8 are the step's own.

dos._source: [C] GUILD.DAT is 22 x 282 bytes; DOSBox s9 filled 22 and silently refused the 23rd (D-002). The DOS manuals state no DOS number: the SSI US manual carries the Apple rulebook's 37, the WizardWorks manual's 21 is in its C64 section.

amiga._source: [~] inferred from file layout: guild.dat is 7050 bytes = 25 x 282, character records 0-21 plus FIRE/WATER/EARTH elementals at 22-24 (DOS takes the elementals from TWNS.INT instead). Fillable maximum not tested in an emulator [?].

apple2._source: Rulebook G)UILD: 'As many as 37 characters can be generated' (SSI US, UK and I+II rulebooks; DIFFERENCES.md D-002 note: the sample Guild list numbers the elementals 38-40).

c64._source: C64 supplement (source-of-truth manual, first page; also the UK and WizardWorks C64 sections): 'A maximum of 21 characters can be generated, and not 37 characters as in the Apple version.' Slot count [?].
